svg.data-what: the wall of the small intestine in section, from the villi to the serosa

rect.data-what: the lumen of the intestine, where digested food passes

path.data-what: the lamina propria: loose connective tissue in the core of each villus and around the crypts, with vessels and immune cells

g.data-what: capillaries in each villus, taking up sugars and amino acids into the blood
lacteals: the lymph vessel at the centre of each villus, taking up fats

path.data-what: the epithelium: one layer of absorptive cells with microvilli, lining the villi and the crypts

g.data-what: goblet cells, scattered in the epithelium, secreting mucus
intestinal crypts: glands between the villi, where stem cells divide to renew the epithelium every few days
villi: finger-like projections, about a millimetre tall, that multiply the absorbing surface

path.data-what: the muscularis mucosae: a thin layer of smooth muscle under the mucosa
the submucosa: connective tissue carrying larger vessels and nerves

g.data-what: the inner circular layer of smooth muscle, squeezing the tube; cut across here
the outer longitudinal layer of smooth muscle, shortening the tube; together the two layers make peristalsis
the myenteric plexus: ganglia of the gut's own nervous system, between the two muscle layers

path.data-what: the serosa: a thin outer membrane covering the intestine
